I was playing Alva in Rail mode when I noticed that the more Shield she has, the closer in damage her Strike and Precision Slash get to each other, which I found strange.

After testing and investigating the character, I realized that her Rouse effect and Soulforge effect do multiply with Base DMG% relics and her Dynamic Vision talent (and DMG Amp as far as I can tell), but her Precision Slash DMG increase effect does not scale with her talent, relics or any other source of Base DMG% and DMG Amp.

You can see this in the attached video where using a Helot Defend to gain 25 Shield only increases Precision Slash's displayed DMG by 50, showing that it is not factoring anything else in besides the pure shield. (The rest of the video is checking that various scalings do work properly, which is good. It is using a borrowed Alva UID 101118720 with about 320% personal Death Resistance stat.)

I checked the Chinese skill texts and asked someone fluent to help me make sure, and we saw that:

3 Cost:
造成 [攻击力×120%] 点伤害。每点护盾使伤害提高 2 点。在本回合中每打出 1 张「防御」，算力消耗 -1。视为「打击」。

Rouse:
艾尔瓦获得 50 点狂气。特殊-图标.png灵知觉醒：获得 [防御力×8%] 点戒备-图标.png戒备。艾尔瓦指令卡造成的伤害随当前护盾提高，每点护盾提高 2。特殊-图标.png保留。

Since the wording is the same and her Rouse & Soulforge do correctly multiply with Base DMG%, I think it is a bug that the +2 DMG per 1 Shield effect of Precision Slash is unaffected by any other stat (it is basically currently "working" as if it was a Strike with added STR = 2×Shield).


-

There is also a slight error with how Alva's Soulforge was translated into English. In Chinese it says;

「打击」和「心眼利刃」造成的基础伤害提高本回合自身获得护盾量的 50%。

Which does say that the base damage is increased based on the shield gained specifically by this character that turn, whereas in English it doesn't specify that - so it reads as if any character on the team providing Shield would increase it (which it doesn't).

Hello there,
I wanted to talk about the character Jenkin, and how she could potentially be improved
upon to have better usage in the current late- to end-game.

To begin with, Jenkin’s current kit is built around giving her a high crit rate and crit damage,
and increasing her damage over time by playing her “Get ‘Em, Brown!” card and a large hit
through her “Mice Assemble”.
The primary issue with this is that her damage increase from herself is through a flat % of her
ATK stat, and nothing else. 

Due to this, her damage increase capacity is very limited in what she can do, as it takes her a while to reach damage levels that other characters can easily hit much faster with the same or less investment. The previous update to her increasing her base dmg by her equipped critical rate value and making “Get ‘Em Brown!” an aoe damage card did help with her temporary lasting ability in the game, but as it currently stands she doesn’t do enough damage to keep up with the health amounts that the newer bosses have, nor does she contribute solid assistance to teams she is on as a support character. 

Other characters that share her role as a standard DPS/carry character have found greater consistency and success in other teams or positions consistently: 
- Liz is a decent poison dps, and can be quite powerful, with fast poison application through the usage of her exalt and cards.
- Nymphaea is almost a staple on most standard poison teams at higher investments, and enables them through her exalt’s trigger.
- While Uvhash isn’t consistently used in higher difficulties of gameplay, he still has powerful scaling capabilities and has managed to still deal large amounts of damage with setup and assistance in longer stages. 
- Helot isn’t as used as a raw carry/DPS, but rather as a reliable support on Strike DMG teams, such as GHelot or Mouchette teams
- Goliath is used on more budget Lemuria/GMurphy teams, and as STR steal/support in other niche areas

Compared to these cases stated above, Jenkin has little to no usage, even with her ability to support various characters through her exalt granting the whole team a sizeable Crit DMG increase for the turn. 

So in summary, I would like to request for a rework or review of Jenkin’s abilities to deal independent damage, as it falls quite short in comparison to other characters who are meant to be performing at the same or at similar levels. While she has never been in the lowest percentage performance or in a position where she has never been used, Jenkin still has always struggled to reach more than a middling level of success.

Here are my suggestions for improving the current D-Tide system based on my experience and the feedback I've seen from other players.

**1. Add 1 more difficulty tier**

There were 5 tiers from A1 to A5. This update compresses them into 2 tiers, Normal and Hard, and adds 2 new tiers, Nightmare and Madness.
The problem is that Normal is too easy while Hard jumps straight to around the old A5 difficulty. This puts people who were comfortable playing A3 or A4 in an awkward situation. Normal is too easy for them, while Hard is too difficult.
Also, before the update, reaching A5 gave players a strong feeling of achievement because it was the highest difficulty. Now, after clearing Hard, they are still at the bottom of the new difficulty system.
So I suggest **adding 1 more tier, something like Easy mode** with difficult of old A1; normal is A2-A3 and hard is A4-A5. This would make the difficulty progression feel much smoother instead of having such a sudden jump. It would also make clearing Hard feel more meaningful, since it would actually be the highest difficulty available to most players before Nightmare.

**2. Adjust the HP of higher difficulties and rebalance the Gaze system**

If I remember correctly, Light said Nightmare's HP would be around 2-3x the current A5 HP. That was before the feedback. After the feedback, he said Nightmare would be adjusted to be more accessible.
However, Nightmare currently has around **4-6x** the HP of Hard. That jump is unnecessarily high, and even whales are struggling to clear Nightmare. Even on Hard, the bosses in W2 and W5 have significantly more HP than usual A5 bosses. I think this needs to be adjusted as soon as possible.
The Gaze system also needs to be rebalanced when mobs have significantly higher HP. You only have 5 turns to chew through all that HP, otherwise your deck gets bricked by a ton of Symptom cards. This basically kills stall teams, because even burst teams can struggle to kill these mobs within 5 turns.

**3. Make the rewards more accessible**

I still believe that whales and veteran players should have additional rewards for clearing the highest difficulties, but it would be better if those rewards were more accessible, as Light promised.
One way to do this would be to **increase the points from extra clears from 5 to 10**. This way, 10 normal = 5 hard, 10 hard = 5 nightmare ...
This would still be a challenge, so it wouldn't take away the reward for players who work hard to clear the higher difficulties. Instead, it gives players more ways to earn the higher-tier rewards without necessarily having to deal with the extreme HP inflation.
It would also make team building more diverse and give more Awakeners a chance to shine, which fits Morimen's motto: **no one gets forgotten.**
These are my 3 suggestions to help fix the current D-Tide system. I hope the devs will consider them. Thanks for reading.
